text:
Noah (sales-eng): Quick thread to capture LuminaHealths asks. They want a POC and an enterprise commit. Traffic is mixed: session-based chat + high-volume vector embeddings. Need guidance on reserved vs autoscale.
Sara (solutions): Do we have a concise traffic snapshot? peak/steady rps, token lengths, embed qps?
Noah (sales-eng): From their intake: steady chat ~80 rps, event peaks up to 1k rps (10-20m windows), avg turn ~220 tokens. Embeddings steady 1.2k qps with flash spikes up to 3k qps for batch indexing. KV cache hit expected ~45%.
Lee (infra): Summary: chat demands low tail latency (p95 target < 350ms) and stateful KV cache. Embeds are throughput-first and tolerate slightly higher latency. Recommendation: reserve a modest baseline for chat (3 GPUs) + elastic pool for embeds (scale-target up to 8 GPUs).
Diego (pricing): For quoting, give me estimated monthly reserved hours and an expected burst-hours range. If they want a single flat-rate commit, we need a break-even analysis vs hybrid.
Sara (solutions): Operational caveats: KV cache warmup will make early minutes of a burst appear worse. Suggest preheat windows around scheduled batches and an indexer agent that can bulk-warm prefixes. Also call out graceful fallback: reserved-chat -> elastic -> quantized-small-model.
Noah (sales-eng): They asked about AZ-level contention. If autoscale fails because of capacity, what's the behavior?
Lee (infra): We can set routing priorities and throttles. Default: route all session requests to reserved pool; if reserved saturated, route new sessions to elastic with higher latency. If both exhausted, fallback to a smaller quantized model (SLA note). Also add per-customer token throttles during embedding floods so chat remains healthy.
Sara (solutions): POC plan to validate:
- 48-hour mixed run, include 4 scheduled 15-20m events simulating 1k chat rps + concurrent 3k embed spikes
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, embed qps sustained, GPU utilization, autoscale reaction times
- One simulated AZ failure to verify cross-AZ fallback and session stickiness recovery
- Quality check on fallback model (sampled prompts)

Noah (sales-eng): Can you draft a conservative autoscale suggestion we can share? Keep knobs tunable.
Lee (infra): Draft config (suggested):
```json
{
  "reserved": { "gpus": "3", "min_instances": "3" },
  "elastic": { "min_instances": "0", "max_instances": "8" },
  "policy": {
    "chat_scale_up_rps": "500",
    "chat_scale_up_cooldown_s": "45",
    "chat_scale_down_rps": "250",
    "chat_scale_down_cooldown_s": "300",
    "embed_scale_threshold_qps": "1500",
    "embed_scale_step": "2"
  },
  "preheat": [{ "cron": "30 08 * * MON,THU", "duration_mins": "25" }]
}
```
Sara (solutions): Add note: ensure model-variant mapping exists (full -> quantized-8bit -> distilled) and that eval thresholds are pre-approved.
Diego (pricing): I'll prepare two quote structures: (A) Hybrid: Reserved 3 GPUs + pay-as-you-go elastic hours; (B) Flat commit: reserve 6 GPUs steady. I'll include an expected monthly burst-hours estimate assuming 6 events/month x 20m + background spikes. Noah, confirm event count.
Noah (sales-eng): They told us 5-8 planned marketing events/month. I'll lock that down in the next call.
Lee (infra): Handoff checklist items to include in the POC doc:
- KV cache TTL and prefix strategy to reach 45% hit target
- Prompts/trace sampling for quality regression detection during fallback
- Canary rollout plan for model updates (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with rollback triggers
- Alerts: p95 chat latency >350ms, embed queue length >3000, autoscale failures, cross-AZ routing errors

Noah (sales-eng): Security ask: KMS for key management and request-level audit logs. sec-bot: any templates?
sec-bot: Link to KMS + audit templates: https://redwood.internal/sec/kms-audit-template (shared).
Sara (solutions): Next steps: I will author the POC runbook (traffic scripts + success criteria). Lee will produce the infra playbook and the autoscale JSON. Diego will attach HYBRID vs FLAT pricing scenarios. Noah will confirm event cadence and share customers staging calendar.
Diego (pricing): ETA: initial numbers by EOD tomorrow.
Lee (infra): I'll also assemble dashboard templates (p95, GPU util, cache hit rate, embed qps).
Noah (sales-eng): Scheduling a 45-min handoff with LuminaHealth tomorrow 11:00 PT. I'll paste the runbook and config here after the call. Thanks all. :rocket:
Sara (solutions): Marking action items: runbook (Sara), infra config & dashboards (Lee), pricing (Diego), schedule + event confirmation (Noah).
Noah (sales-eng): end of thread
